The simultaneous improvement of mechanical and corrosion resistance is of great significance for engineering applications. In this work, a novel lightweight amorphous structure AlTiVNb high-entropy alloy (HEA) film was fabricated by magnetron sputtering. The compression test of the AlTiVNb HEA film nanopillar exhibits a high compressive strength of up to 3.6 GPa and deformability approaching 58%. The high strength is affected by the disordered state, the nanostructure, and the lattice distortion effect, while the high ductility comes from the ductile shear band and the island structure. In addition, the AlTiVNb HEA film shows a current density of 4.90 × 10−8 A/cm2 and a potential of −0.234 V in the 3.5% NaCl solution, comparable to that of the 316L stainless steel. The chemical disorder state, cocktail effect, and homogeneous amorphous structure contribute to excellent corrosion resistance. This finding offers new insights into high-performance HEA films with robust mechanical and anticorrosion performances for microelectronic devices and mechanical metamaterials.

decision.trend: Research on high-entropy alloys has been focused on understanding their mechanical properties, corrosion resistance, and wear resistance. Earlier studies have investigated the effects of different alloying elements, processing methods, and environmental conditions on the properties of high-entropy alloys. Recently, there has been a trend towards exploring the potential of high-entropy alloys in extreme environments, such as high-temperature and corrosive conditions. The use of advanced characterization techniques, such as scanning transmission electron microscopy and atomistic simulations, has also become more prevalent in the field.
decision.unsolved: Despite the progress made in understanding high-entropy alloys, there is still a lack of a single mechanistic hypothesis that can explain the resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in these materials. The complex interactions between the alloying elements, the microstructure, and the environmental conditions make it challenging to develop a comprehensive understanding of the underlying mechanisms.
